title: Why TSMC Is Letting Go of CoWoS—and Where Its Real Second Moat Lies
gist: A short forum repost of a Liang-rong Chen piece arguing TSMC is deliberately conceding share of CoWoS AI-chip packaging to ASE, Amkor and Intel's EMIB-T while relocating its moat to SoIC 3D stacking, the technology Nvidia is expected to use for its future Feynman GPU.

themes.theme: TSMC moat migration: CoWoS to SoIC

insights.claim: TSMC is voluntarily ceding a larger share of CoWoS advanced packaging to ASE and Amkor rather than defending its near-monopoly, signalling that CoWoS is no longer the packaging technology it considers defensible.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Watch OSAT order books (ASE, Amkor) for CoWoS share gains that come without a TSMC price war — margin-accretive volume rather than a share fight.
insights.quote: TSMC has spent years building CoWoS into an almost unassailable position in AI chip packaging. So why is it now willing to let ASE and Amkor take a bigger piece of the business?
insights.locator: TSMC has spent years building CoWoS

insights.claim: TSMC is shifting its packaging focus to SoIC, a more demanding 3D stacking technology, which is where the article argues its real second moat now lies.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: SoIC capacity build and hybrid-bonding tool orders become the leading indicator of TSMC's packaging pricing power, not CoWoS capacity.
insights.quote: TSMC is shifting its focus toward SoIC, a far more demanding 3D stacking technology
insights.locator: As CoWoS-like packaging spreads across the industry

insights.claim: Nvidia is expected to adopt TSMC's SoIC 3D stacking for its future Feynman generation of GPUs.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: If Feynman requires SoIC, TSMC keeps the highest-value step of the Nvidia supply chain even as CoWoS commoditizes — a reason not to read OSAT share gains as TSMC weakness.
insights.quote: SoIC, a far more demanding 3D stacking technology that Nvidia is expected to adopt for its future Feynman GPU
insights.locator: As CoWoS-like packaging spreads across the industry

insights.claim: CoWoS-like 2.5D packaging is diffusing across the industry, with ASE investing billions in advanced packaging and Amkor bringing CoWoS capacity to the United States.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Multi-sourced CoWoS relieves the AI-accelerator packaging bottleneck and caps pricing upside for the technology — a volume story for OSATs, not a scarcity rent.
insights.quote: ASE is pouring billions into advanced packaging, Amkor is bringing CoWoS to the U.S.

insights.claim: Intel's EMIB-T is breaking into packaging territory once dominated by TSMC, adding a third credible supplier of high-end 2.5D interconnect.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: An Intel packaging win is a rare tangible proof point for Intel Foundry; track EMIB-T customer announcements as an Intel re-rating catalyst.
insights.quote: even Intel’s EMIB-T is breaking into territory once dominated by TSMC

insights.claim: TSMC is not exiting advanced packaging but choosing which battlefield to defend, a framework for reading any incumbent's apparent share concession as a moat relocation rather than a retreat.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Apply the same test to other TSMC concessions: ask whether the ceded step still carries pricing power or whether the rent has already moved one layer up.
insights.quote: TSMC isn’t walking away from advanced packaging. It may simply be deciding which battlefield is worth defending.
